teks: If you stacked a billion dollars in hundred-dollar bills, how tall would the pile be?
Guess first! A, 11 meters. B, 110 meters. Or C, 1,100 meters.
A billion dollars in hundred-dollar bills is 10 million bills.
Assume each bill is 0.11 millimeters thick.
So 10 million times 0.11 millimeters gives 1,100 meters.
The Burj Khalifa, the tallest building on Earth, is only 828 meters. The answer is C, a stack of cash taller than the Burj Khalifa!
